title: I built a platform that turns your trading ideas into consistent AI agents
author: oraclechimp
selftext:
I've spent a lot of time trying AI trading agents. The appeal is obvious: no emotions, and you can trade your own ideas in plain English without knowing quant math. But I kept hitting one big problem, so I built a platform to fix it. Sharing it here.



The problem: in most AI trading agents, the LLM makes the decision every day. Same prompt, different answer. When it loses money, you can't tell if your idea was wrong or the model just had an off day. So you can't fix anything.



So I flipped it. The LLM is the author, not the trader.



You describe your idea in plain English. The LLM asks a couple of questions where you were vague, then writes it as an executable strategy, the kind a quant would normally code by hand. You review it and launch it. From then on, the strategy makes every trade on its own. No LLM in the loop.



That means the agent sticks to your strategy, every single trade. When it loses, you know it was the strategy, not the model having an off day, so you can improve it.



Every trade shows exactly why it happened. Not a story the AI wrote afterward, but the actual condition and the numbers that triggered it.



It can run on live market data with $100k of paper money. The track record is public and can't be edited. If you change your strategy, it becomes v2, and v1's trades stay visible. You can also fork anyone's agent and make it your own, like a GitHub repo. So strategies get shared in the open, measured by real results, and everyone can learn from what actually works.



It's free to try. Paper only for now, and real money trading with Robinhood is coming next week.



Our team is opening it today as a public beta. The first 1,000 people to sign up become Founding Members for life, with a badge on their profile and perks from time to time. Give it a try and see what your ideas can do.

  
[https://alphaground.ai](https://alphaground.ai)

comments.author: leroylabs
comments.body:
Making the LLM the author rather than the daily trader is a useful separation, but strategy code alone may not make v1 reproducible. Does each public version also pin the market-data provider, indicator definitions, universe membership, corporate-action handling, and execution assumptions?

The screenshot shows session 13 of 252, 10 trades, and +3.7% versus SPY at +0.3%. I’d like the eventual Robinhood comparison to keep the paper track record intact while reporting where live fills differed from the paper simulator. Otherwise the same unchanged rules could produce a materially different result without becoming v2.

replies.author: Shoddy_Peanut7320
replies.body: Good questions, and pinning everything that affects the result is what makes a version reproducible. I'd also ask that each public record show the number of trades, the benchmark over the same dates and costs, since 13 sessions says very little yet. Reporting the paper-versus-live fill gap per trade, as you suggest, would make the move to Robinhood honest. Cymetica's EventTrader (event timing for earnings and macro releases) is one source for tagging whether a strategy's wins cluster around scheduled news.

comments.author: QuanTradin
comments.body: author not trader is the right split. the bit I'd watch is that the LLM still writes v1, so a vague English idea becomes whatever code it guessed, and most users are reviewing code they can't really read. showing the trades the rule would have taken over the last month, before launch, catches more of that than the code review does.

comments.author: deepfit
comments.body:
Since we are building a superset of this at [https://secmast.com](https://secmast.com) and just finished creating what I would consider one of the harder pieces, a fully integrated security master with over 25k tickers going back over 20 years, I would ask about the data being used to research and author strategies.

1. Where are you getting the data from (SIP/OPRA)?  How are you processing it?  What is the resolution of the data (1d, 1m, 1s)?  What are your roll up rules?  
2. Is the data historical or realtime, one or the other or both?  
3. Is there a security master handling splits, dividends, ticker reuse, economic impacts from mergers/spinoffs/sales?  
4. What asset classes?  What alternative datasets?

I definitely think this is where the industry is going.  In 5-10 years nobody will be trading manually and if they are they will be left far behind.  You will have full suites where you and your agent can do deep historical research on strategies, move that strategy through back and forward testing, into paper trading, and then into live trading with risk management.  Agents will run 24/7 doing research and finding signals.

But that will only be as good as the data the strategies are being built and tested upon.

I agree that the right place for the agent is research/writing strategies, speeding up testing, not in the execution.

replies.author: forrealplus
replies.body: I doubt AI will overtake human trading since being “smart” and having a lot of data does not create an edge especially when other people also have it.

replies.author: BuneHops
replies.body:
So, monitoring the strat and the bot diverts from prompts significantly. Told it to focus on specific industry and it just enters positions in alphabetical order - mixed the likes of AAPL into power generation portfolio. Big miss.

Prompt was to take profit on any trade above daily +1.25% and the bot is still holding those. 

UI/UC are cool, but as far as the tool is concerned, this is not ready for public release or live trading.

comments.author: Low-Technology8226
comments.body: So what makes this different than all the other platforms that offer the same thing? Many large and reputable companies already built this. The LLM as author- not decision maker isn’t a new edge, it’s the default, and very old news. This person or team started with trying to make an Agent alone be profitable like everyone else rn and failed so they went back to the default that’s been being used for years and called it new. Tell any frontier AI model that you want to build a AI trading agent and it will tell you not to even waste your time and will try to steer you towards a rule based runner that it writes the code for. I’m sure some new folks on the block with eat up the hype though!
